issues.on_page: Intergovernmental 8,411,742 (Exhibit 4); B-3 p15 Motor vehicle tax 308,350, Federal - FEMA 17,712, Federal funds police assistance 45,645, Federal - Other Grants 212,732; B-4 p19 Federal grants 2,862,398; C-1 p21 Federal grants 83,355; E-4 p25 CDBG 334,535
issues.issue: The fund schedules give the full breakdown of this line: General 2,389,146 + Airport 2,862,398 = 5,251,544, Streets 2,407,859, and Other Governmental 334,535 + 155 + 378,150 + 39,499 = 752,339. The extractor used that breakdown to split out Pro-Rate 7,962, but the remainder still holds motor vehicle tax 308,350 (its own receipt category) and federal grants 3,556,377 (about 42%). State and local aid is the larger part (about 54%), so the dominant-category rule makes this defensible, but splitting out motor vehicle tax and federal grants would match how pro-rate was handled.

issues.on_page: Occupation tax 581,491 = B-3 p15 Utilities occupation 422,888 + Beer and liquor 23,165 + Lodging occupation tax 132,485 + Miscellaneous occupation 2,953
issues.issue: This line includes lodging occupation tax 132,485 (23%), which has its own category (lodging tax) and is itemized on p15. Property tax was split using the same schedule but this line was not. Occupation tax is still the dominant part, so this is defensible, but the handling is inconsistent.

'Customer accounting expenses' is a utility function or account group (billing and collection), not a cost type. The cost-type rule applies only to lines printed by cost type, so 'utilities' (like Operating and maintenance and Administrative and general) may fit better.

'Operating contracts' reads like a cost type (contracted services), which under the 2026-10-28 utility cost-type rule would be Professional/Contract Services with function utilities. Meanwhile 'Engineering services' (disbursements[13]) was given that cost-type category. The two are handled differently.

issues.extracted: Improvements other than buildings (category capital outlay)
issues.on_page: Capital Outlay: Improvements other than buildings 3,320,960
issues.issue: This line is in category capital outlay but was not relabelled 'Capital Outlay: Airport' (printed text in printed_label). The Buildings line under the same heading (detail[122]) was relabelled. The same relabel is missing on the other capital outlay detail lines: E-3 detail[159] and E-4 detail[164] 'Capital outlay', G-3 detail[180]-[181] police and fire equipment, and G-4 detail[187]-[195]. user_rules.py may handle these.

issues.on_page: E-2 p23 and Exhibit 4 p6 report Economic Development 589,605 and CDBG Grant distributions 332,305 as General government
issues.issue: The detail function (economic development, also detail[163]) follows the E-3/E-4 labels, but the report's own combining statement and governmental funds statement count these amounts as general government. So detail by function won't tie to the statement's general government 953,448 (944,073 + G-4 9,375). Defensible either way.
'not itemized' is meant for a function or department total with no object breakdown. A contingency line inside an itemized department is closer to 'miscellaneous expenditure'.

issues.on_page: Restitution - fees and damages 3,397 (printed under Charges for Services)
issues.issue: Restitution for damages could also be reimbursements/refunds. This is a judgment call.

issues.on_page: Repairs and maintenance supplies 17,413 (printed under Supplies)
issues.issue: The same label in Streets C-1 (detail[146]) is 'supplies and materials'. The rules say to use the same category for the same label within a report, and on p19 this line is printed under the Supplies heading.

issues.on_page: E-6 911 Surcharge: Capital outlay actual - (0), final budget 75,000
issues.issue: This zero-actual line was omitted and the notes don't mention it. The notes list only the G-4 zero lines (Public building improvements, Lodging tax projects), and other zero lines (B-4 Buildings, Contingency) were recorded. There is no effect on the amounts.
